The application of force on integrins triggers cytoskeletal rearrangements and growth of the… 10991183 the-rho-gefs-larg-and-gef-h1-regulate-the-mechanical-response-to-force-on-integrins rho gefs larg gef h1 regulate mechanical response How individual cells respond to mechanical forces is of considerable interest to biologists as force affects many as The Rho GEFs LARG and GEF-H1 regulate the mechanical response to force on integrins How individual cells respond to mechanical forces is of considerable interest to biologists as force affects many aspects of cell behaviour. The application of force on integrins triggers cytoskeletal rearrangements and growth of the associated adhesion complex, resulting in increased cellular stiffness, also known as reinforcement. Although RhoA has been shown to play a role during reinforcement, the molecular mechanisms that regulate its activity are unknown. By combining biochemical and biophysical approaches, we identified two guanine nucleotide exchange factors (GEFs), LARG and GEF-H1, as key molecules that regulate the cellular adaptation to force.
